I just wrote this as a response to the question of who wears watches anymore. I believe it stands on its own as an explanation of why watches are so special. I think it is worth the repost here to open up a discussion about why YOU wear a watch.

"As prices of used watches show, quite a few people wear them. There has been a definite resurgence, and it basically boils down to two types of people. Enthusiasts of watches and horology, and enthusiasts of fashion. You will see some crossover, but generally a watch enthusiast is not going to buy a fashion brand such as Hilfiger or Fossil. Someone who is in it just for an accessory probably does not care about owning a mechanical watch over a quartz. Sometimes people who just like having it as an accessory start to appreciate watches for beyond just a fashion statement.

It is not about being able to see the time at a glance, though there is utility to a watch. A watch is one of the only acceptable pieces of jewelry for men to wear. A watch reflects the wearer's personality and appreciation of classical machinery that is lost in today's digital world. Putting on a watch is an opportunity to further personalize your appearance, not just in the sense of "looking good" but as a reminder of what role you want to play that day. Maybe it's the weekend, and you are having a casual stroll through the park. Well, that is a perfect opportunity to immerse yourself in that and wear a sport watch such as a diver or chronograph. Feeling dressy? A nice simple thin watch tucked under the shirt cuff is just one more element of your attire to make you feel confident. A watch could be a status symbol, something to clue others in that you are a man of taste and refinement. But more than that, it is a reminder to oneself of where you come from, where you are, and where you want to be going.

A mechanical watch is a marvel of engineering, and there is something special about the tactile feel of winding the crown, or hearing the subtle grind of an automatic as you move your wrist. Watches harken back to a simpler time when men were men and women were women. A quality mechanical watch is an heirloom piece that you could pass down to your son, and he to his. If maintained, it could run indefinitely. It will not go obsolete, lost under a constant stream of software updates and hardware refreshes. Long after the computer I am writing this on is all but useless, my watches could still be wound and perform their duty.

We live in a society that is a throwaway culture, but wearing a watch is a symbol of ever enduring humanity and the marvels we could build. Watches are something special, they say you don't really ever own a mechanical watch, you are just holding it for whoever gets it next. There is a comfort in that."

So that is why I believe watches are important, and why some watches are so valuable. Do you wear a watch? Why?
Why we wear watches - why do you?
